name: Copper (Crayola)
lede: Copper (Crayola) is a muted orange-brown from Crayola's crayon list, named for the metal but noticeably lighter and pinker than metallic copper itself.

sections.title: A crayon named for a metal
sections.body: Our record of this name traces to Wikipedia's inventory of Crayola crayon colors, which names it as a Crayola variant of [[copper]] rather than citing a dictionary or standard [1]. Crayola does not publish when the crayon entered the box or who chose it, so both are undocumented here [1]. The parenthetical "(Crayola)" marks it apart from the plainer, more metallic [[copper]] in our library [1]. Its nearest named neighbors by color distance are [[onion-skin-pink|Onion-Skin Pink]], a duller rose at 3.6 units, and [[dark-peach|Dark Peach]], a more vivid version at 3.8 [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color this close to Copper (Crayola) is unusually common in our archive: 212 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, about 0.89 percent, more common than 64 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1500s, at 2.2 times the expected rate, and it is most often an accent, in 71 percent of its matches [3]. Amedeo Modigliani is its most devoted painter, carrying it in four of his eighteen works here, 5.7 times the baseline for the museums those paintings come from [3]. The earliest match dates to 1150, long before Crayola existed [3]. That is centuries before the name's own record, a floor on the hue's age, not a first use of either the name or a pigment.
